decision.state: Promising intervention; organization-level marginal cost-effectiveness not yet estimable
decision.summary: Project Open Hand directly delivered interventions studied in randomized trials, which is stronger organization-specific evidence than most local discovery records. Results are mixed across populations and outcomes, and reviewed public sources do not isolate the current cost or counterfactual outcomes of the next philanthropic gift.

financialContext.summary: The FY2024 audit reports $13.47 million in total assets and $6.91 million available for general expenditure within one year.
financialContext.boundary: Audited organization-wide amounts are capacity and liquidity context. They are not the cost of the medically tailored meal intervention, unrestricted surplus, or room for more funding.

evidence.population: 1,977 recently hospitalized high-risk adults in Northern California; Project Open Hand and Ceres delivered meals
evidence.result: The primary all-cause 90-day readmission outcome was not improved: 27.1% with meals versus 24.6% usual care; adjusted hazard ratio 1.02 (95% CI 0.86–1.21). Exploratory analyses found lower heart-failure hospitalization among participants with heart failure and lower all-cause mortality, but no all-cause emergency-department benefit.
evidence.transfer: Direct delivery involvement supports implementation relevance, but results combine two providers and multiple counties; exploratory outcomes should not replace the null primary result.

evidence.population: 191 Project Open Hand clients living with HIV; intensive food-plus-nutrition support versus less-intensive Project Open Hand standard care
evidence.result: At six months, the intensive arm had lower odds of hospitalization, food insecurity, depressive symptoms, poor antiretroviral adherence, and unprotected sex. The trial found no difference in its primary viral-nonsuppression or health-related-quality-of-life outcomes.
evidence.transfer: Organization-specific and locally relevant, but small, population-specific, and a comparison of two service intensities—not food support versus no service.

evidence.population: Medi-Cal beneficiaries with congestive heart failure across eight California counties; Project Open Hand served San Francisco, Alameda, and San Mateo
evidence.result: The intervention offered three meals daily for 12 weeks plus nutrition therapy and case-management components. The evaluation is useful for implementation and claims-based outcome context but does not publish a Project Open Hand-only causal estimate.
evidence.transfer: Provider-pooled results cannot be assigned to Project Open Hand, and program components and payer reimbursement may differ from a marginal philanthropic expansion.

model.nativeOutcome: Avoided condition-specific hospitalization over a defined follow-up period
missingInputs: A named current Project Open Hand program and eligible cohort for the marginal gift
Full incremental cost per enrolled and completed participant, including shared costs
Expected enrollment, completion, displacement, and payer-reimbursement case
A pre-specified causal effect applicable to that cohort rather than selected exploratory outcomes
Independent confirmation of which outcomes Project Open Hand can report for the funded cohort
model.qalyBoundary: No QALY, WELLBY, life-saved, or life-substantially-bettered conversion is published. A condition-specific avoided-hospitalization model must come first.

reservations: The largest reviewed randomized trial missed its primary outcome; favorable mortality and heart-failure findings were exploratory.
The smaller HIV trial found no effect on its primary viral or health-related-quality-of-life outcomes.
FY2024 scale combines several programs and three counties, so dividing organization expenses by meals or clients would be misleading.
Public financing and reimbursement may fund some medically tailored nutrition; the philanthropic counterfactual and displacement case are not published.
No current organization-supplied marginal plan was found in the reviewed public sources.
